newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq protests over alleged Turkish violations.
newsitem.headline: Iraq protests over alleged Turkish violations.

text.p: Iraq on Tuesday protested to the United Nations against what it termed "violations of Iraq's airspace and territory by Turkish troops", the official Iraqi news agency INA said.

It quoted a letter sent by Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali as saying: "The Turkish troops' shelling of Iraq's villages and towns in the north and entering illegally to its territory represent a flagrant violation of Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity."
Sahaf urged Ankara to end the mandate of U.S. and allied forces policing a no-fly zone in northern Iraq.
"The presence of the so-called 'Hammer Forces' on Turkish territory under various allegations is only meant to render hostile acts against Iraq and interfere in its internal affairs," he said.
He urged Turkey to "review its policy toward northern Iraq and set up cooperation between the two neighbouring countries".
Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz arrived on an impromptu visit to the Turkish capital for talks with senior officials on Tuesday.

Ankara last month hosted U.S.-sponsored talks between Iraq's warring Kurdish factions, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK). The talks halted fighting between them which started in August, when Baghdad sent troops to back the KDP against its rival the PUK.
Baghdad criticised Turkey for hosting the talks.
